items.claim: stockanalysis (20 Nov 14:10 ET): Ming-Chi Kuo (TF International Securities), citing his latest industry survey, says Google is trimming 2027 shipments of its TPU 8i series by about 1m units, roughly 20%, with most of the cut falling on the pricier 8i Max ('Whalefish'); Google plans to ship more TPU 8t (MediaTek-designed) instead; details are not final; Kuo tied the shift to 'frontier model development gets first call on compute', a tight supply chain and data-centre power constraints; neither company commented; Alphabet shares flat; AVGO -11.4% at 14:09 ET amid SOX -8.0%, NDX -3.7%, S&P -2.1%, MU -11.4%, AMD -11.2%, MRVL -9.2%, NVDA -7.1%; MediaTek -10% in Taipei (trading ended before the post); 10y fell from 5.05% to 4.94%; no dollar revenue impact estimated. 247wallst (20 Nov 14:13 ET): Kuo described it as 'an adjustment to tight supply and limited data center power'; AVGO ~-12% to 306.55 at 13:43 ET vs 346.65 Thursday close, ~USD 191bn lost, heading for its worst day since 4 Jun, 36% below its 2 Jun record 481.57; Broadcom bought USD 1bn of Anthropic at USD 83; Hock Tan 2 Sep: 'our engagement with Google has never been stronger', TPU 8i production shipments started and would ramp to high volumes, Anthropic 'on track to become our largest XPU customer in 2027'. cappnotes close: AVGO -12.19%. Still the first in-gate order-cut headline on GOOGL/AVGO and the market priced it as a cut (-12%, USD 191bn). Verification points: Broadcom FQ4 call 9 Dec; Alphabet Q4 capex guide late Jan. It's Nvidia's Worst Day Since DeepSeek and It Has Lost $2.7 Trillion Since October / Here's Why Nvidia Stock Crashed on Friday
items.claim: Reuters via investing.com (20 Nov 14:16, updated 16:06): two people briefed on the matter said SEC enforcement staff are looking at 'potential accounting issues' at Nvidia; Reuters could not determine when the inquiry opened or what issues it covers; investigations 'are not evidence of wrongdoing'; Nvidia did not immediately respond, SEC declined to comment; shares were down ~13% Friday per LSEG after the report, having fallen >6% before it, and down more than a third in the broader crisis; on Tuesday's call interim CEO Colette Kress said the company would be 'far more selective' about AI financing deals; background: Huang 'ousted' after an 8 Nov statement admitting an affair, US authorities suspect Alice Huang - formerly head of Singapore-based Megaspeed, a historically large Nvidia customer under export-control investigation since 2024 - is a Chinese spy (China denies); Nvidia last year switched geographic revenue reporting to customer HQ, removing Singapore (FT: Singapore sales had risen to almost half of revenue); DOJ reviewing the USD 12.9bn Hugging Face acquisition and a broader antitrust investigation. 247wallst (15:17 ET): ~USD 431bn lost Friday, ~USD 2.7tn since the October record, ~USD 900bn on the week, 46% below the 6 Oct record close 239.24, market value ~USD 3.1tn; Q3 revenue USD 115.8bn, USD 130bn guide, first report without Huang; stock rose after hours on the report 'and has fallen every day since'. items.headline: Fed's Cook says rate hikes needed to lower high inflation (Reuters via Kitco) / Fed governor admits people see higher inflation as normal, vows to break that 'kind of psychology' (Fortune)
items.claim: Reuters via Kitco (20 Nov 13:31 EST): in a speech prepared for a central-bank conference in Chile, Cook said the Fed's policy rate is not high enough to address inflation, that 'waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve', that 'we do not have that luxury' of patience, that the September quarter-point hike was not enough, that there is 'little evidence inflation is declining' and recent data fail to provide 'sufficient evidence that inflation is returning to a sustainable path' after more than five and a half years above target; growth 'strong and accelerating', labour market 'solid'; financial conditions remain accommodative; acting too late could force larger later hikes that 'could increase stress on our financial system'; she dissented in October when the Fed held at 3.75-4.00%. Fortune (20 Nov 16:08 ET): Cook on Friday said 'every additional day poses greater risk that price- and wage-setters will adjust their inflation expectations upward'; CME FedWatch fully prices a 25bp December hike; a 50bp move would take the range to 4.25-4.50%; Chair Warsh has opposed forward guidance. cappnotes: Paulson open to back-to-back hikes; Kalshi 25bp 90% / hold 9% / larger 2%.

items.headline: Fed's Waller doubles down on a jumbo rate hike in December, sees more hikes to come
items.claim: Yahoo Finance / Schonberger (18 Nov 09:46 PST): Waller said on CNBC that if the Fed raises 25bp next month it needs to clearly signal another 25bp in January, otherwise 'you have to go 50 in December'; 'it only affects market pricing if you signal you're going to do it'; the signal could come in the statement, at Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference, or via December's quarterly projections; the Fed 'may need to do more' and should reverse last year's three cuts; inflation has been above 2% for nearly six years; October CPI +0.4% (vs 0.3% expected), core +0.3% (vs 0.2%); Williams: 'I don't think the situation calls for dramatic action'; Warsh, chair since May, has sought to eliminate forward guidance. Fortune (20 Nov) quoting the same interview: 'People are starting to think 3% may be the norm', 'that's the kind of psychology we need to start breaking', 'We can't wait. We can't do this in like the next two years', 'So we may have to go above... three hikes plus maybe some more to get it to start actually coming back down'; a 50bp move would take the range to 4.25-4.50% from 3.75-4.00%.
